implementation_notes: The enumeration message is the range-based for statement: the collection exposes begin()/end() (members or free functions found by ADL) and the loop dereferences each iterator for the body, which cppreference describes as the readable equivalent of the traditional for loop over a range. std::for_each - and since C++20 std::ranges::for_each - is the message form where the action is a value rather than a statement; the transforming messages live in <algorithm>/<numeric> and, since C++20, in the ranges adaptors. Index loops stay appropriate where the position itself is part of the computation.
pitfalls: The range must outlive the loop: range-for over a container returned by value binds to a temporary, and the loop iterates a dangling reference when no lifetime extension applies.
Modifying the container from the body invalidates the iterators - adding to a std::vector reallocates and erasing while iterating is undefined behaviour; use erase-remove or collect-then-apply.
auto deduces by value, so for (auto x : c) copies every element; write const auto& (or auto&& in generic code) unless the copy is intended.

variants.name: Iterator pair with the algorithms library (classic)
variants.idiom_name: std::for_each over c.begin(), c.end() with a function object
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-C++11 form of the pattern: the walk is the free function std::for_each(first, last, f), the action is a function object or plain function pointer, and the collection contributes only its iterator pair - the container/iterator/algorithm decomposition the standard library was built on. The transforming cases use the same shape (std::accumulate and friends), so the structure survives in code that must stay C++03-clean; the cost is a named functor type for every distinct action.
pitfalls: The algorithm takes the functor by value: mutations to the copy are invisible afterwards, so state must flow through a reference_wrapper or a returned result.
Iterator invalidation applies exactly as in a manual loop - modifying the container inside the action invalidates first/last, and the bug is silent for node-based containers.

variants.name: Ranges pipeline over lazy views
variants.implementation_notes: C++20 supplies the transforming messages as range adaptors: views compose lazily into a view that is walked once at the terminal step (a range-for or std::ranges::for_each), so no intermediate container is built and concepts check the action's signature at compile time. Choose it where the toolchain is C++20 and the walk is a pipeline rather than one side-effecting loop; the view's lifetime is the price of the laziness.
pitfalls: A view borrows the range it was built from: composing a pipeline over a temporary container (a by-value return) leaves it dangling, so the container must outlive the walk or be materialised.
A view over a const range yields const references; an action that must mutate elements needs a non-const range, and the compiler's error appears at the adaptor, not at the mutation.
